newsitem.title: INDIA: India needs 4.5 pct farm growth to reach target.
newsitem.headline: India needs 4.5 pct farm growth to reach target.

text.p: India's agriculture sector must grow by 4.5 percent during the ninth five-year plan (1997-2002) to achieve a target of seven percent overall, a senior Agriculture Ministry official said on Thursday.

"Our agriculture sector has to grow by 4.5 percent in the ninth plan to achieve the targeted growth rate of seven percent," K. Rajan, the highest-ranking civil servant in the ministry told a news conference.
The Planning Commission, the country's highest planning body, has set an economic growth target of seven percent during the ninth plan, which began on April 1.
India's relatively centralised planned economy uses five-year plans to set government spending priorities.
Rajan said better technology management, input management and water management is needed to achieve the growth rate.
Despite unseasonal rains in the northern states last week, wheat production was likely to "show a good recovery" in the current 1996/97 season, Rajan said.
India's 1996/97 (June-May) wheat crop is estimated at 64.66 million tonnes compared with 62.62 million tonnes the previous year, the Agriculture Ministry said in a statement.
